sources.entry: LMS - Access your self-hosted music using a web interface. GPL-3.0 Docker/deb/C++

summary.one_liner: LMS (Lightweight Music Server) is a self-hosted music streaming server with a web interface for accessing your music collection from anywhere.
summary.what_it_does: LMS scans music libraries and organizes them mainly by tags such as genre, mood, artists, and release types, with support for MusicBrainz identifiers. It exposes a Subsonic/OpenSubsonic API and provides a web interface for browsing, searching, and playing tracks. It includes a recommendation engine (audio-similarity via MusicNN embeddings, or tag-based), radio mode, and discovery filters such as recently added or most played by genre. It also handles podcasts, playlists (m3u/m3u8), lyrics (lrc, txt, embedded), ReplayGain, audio transcoding, multi-library support, and scrobbling to ListenBrainz and Last.fm. A demo instance is available, though administration settings are disabled there.
use_cases: Stream my self-hosted music collection from a browser
Use a Subsonic-compatible client with my own music server
Discover music by genre, mood, or tags
Scrobble listens to ListenBrainz or Last.fm
Manage playlists and podcasts for a music library
Organize a music collection with MusicBrainz IDs and artwork
how_to_run: See INSTALL.md file in the repository
notable: Audio-similarity recommendations using MusicNN embeddings, or tag-based recommendations
Artist information folder following Kodi's structure (artist.nfo) and .lmsignore exclusion files
Detailed artwork lookup rules using MusicBrainz IDs, with fallback to embedded images
Jukebox support and multiple authentication backends
caveats: Audio-similarity recommendation extraction speed depends on scanner threads and storage speed (roughly 1k to 25k tracks/hour reported)
Demo instance does not expose administration settings
Installation details are in a separate INSTALL.md, not in the README
